extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewing WACV 2026 submissions, including distinct evaluation criteria for two paper types (application vs algorithms) plus expectations about review quality, ethics, conflicts of interest, and enforcement. Reviewers should apply the listed criteria when assessing submissions and when composing reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems-level innovation (Application papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application papers will be evaluated on systems-level innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application papers focus on innovation at the systems/application level; reviewers should value systems contributions even if algorithmic novelty is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of the domain (Application papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application papers will be evaluated on novelty of the domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper applies methods to a novel domain or context; novelty of domain is a positive evaluation axis distinct from algorithmic novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative assessment (Application papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application papers will be evaluated on comparative assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for comparisons against relevant baselines or existing systems within the applied domain; comparative evaluation is important for application papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not evaluate application papers solely on algorithmic novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Application papers should NOT be evaluated solely on the basis of algorithmic novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable for application papers to have little or no algorithmic novelty; reviewers should weigh systems-level contribution, domain novelty, and comparative assessment appropriately rather than applying only algorithm-focused criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic novelty (Algorithms papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithms papers will be evaluated according to algorithmic novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For algorithm papers, novelty in the algorithmic contribution is a primary evaluation axis; novelty should be clearly articulated and contextualized relative to prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantified evaluation against current alternatives (Algorithms papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithms papers will be evaluated on quantified evaluation against current, alternative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require rigorous, quantitative comparisons to current baselines/alternatives. Empirical evaluation should be sufficient to support claims of improvement or advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair and thoughtful reviews (Responsible reviewing expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are expected to provide fair and thoughtful reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat authors' work respectfully and evaluate based on the content. The policy gives examples of highly irresponsible behavior to illustrate failures of fairness and thoughtfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: No one-sentence reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: One-sentence reviews are considered highly irresponsible behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be substantive; single-sentence feedback is insufficient to justify scores or to be useful to authors or program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reviews generated by Large Language Models (LLMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) are considered highly irresponsible behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews must reflect the reviewer's own assessment and engagement; using LLMs to generate reviews is prohibited per the stated expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submission of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews submitted late are considered highly irresponsible behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must meet reviewing deadlines; late reviews violate the Reviewing Deadline Policy and can trigger enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the paper's actual content
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews that lack engagement with the paper's actual content are considered highly irresponsible behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should read and consider the actual claims, experiments, and arguments in the submission rather than making superficial or irrelevant comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and protection of authors' ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: As a reviewer for WACV, you have the responsibility to protect the confidentiality of the ideas represented in the papers you review. WACV submissions are not published documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat submissions as new/proprietary work. Do not disclose, share, or use authors' unpublished ideas outside the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict enforcement policy and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: WACV will strictly enforce a Responsible Reviewing Policy and a Reviewing Deadline Policy; non-compliance may lead to consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reviewer whose review fails to comply with these policies may face possible desk rejection of all papers on which they are an author. Take the policies seriously to avoid sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest — same institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Common conflicts include same institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you share the same institution with authors, declare the conflict and do not review the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest — recent collaborators (within 3 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common conflicts include recent collaborators (within 3 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decline to review papers where you have collaborated with authors within the last 3 years to avoid bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest — advisor/advisee relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Common conflicts include advisor/advisee relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisor/advisee ties are conflicts; reviewers should not handle such papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest — family members
rubrics_metrics.description: Common conflicts include family members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal family relationships constitute a conflict and should be declared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest — close personal relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Common conflicts include close personal relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close personal relationships that could affect impartiality should be declared and avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage substantively with the paper's content (Review quality standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each review should engage substantively with the paper's content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed discussion of the paper's methods, experiments, claims, and limitations rather than cursory remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify both strengths and weaknesses (Review quality standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each review should identify both strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balanced reviews point out what the paper does well as well as shortcomings, so authors and chairs can make informed decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific, actionable feedback (Review quality standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each review should provide specific, actionable feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete suggestions for improvements (e.g., additional experiments to run, clearer baselines, clarifications) rather than vague criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify scores with concrete reasoning (Review quality standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each review should justify scores with concrete reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores must be accompanied by evidence and reasoning drawn from the paper; do not assign scores without explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a professional tone (Review quality standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each review should maintain a professional tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ad hominem language, sarcasm, or unprofessional remarks. Reviews should be respectful and constructive.
